headline: ARY does not need to invent a services business — it already has the SKUs sitting unused in its own catalogue ("Xerox Charges" and "Delivery Charges" have literally never been billed, 0 sales ever), and the one service it does run, tailoring through 18 contract tailors, has earned a 2.9% gross margin over 3.4 years on ₹15.79 L of revenue while attaching to only 13.9% of the fabric it sells; fixing what exists is worth more than any new licence, and the two bank branches physically at Baru Sahib (SBI SBIN0011784, PNB PUNB0975500) kill the AePS/banking-correspondent idea that looks most attractive from the outside.

findings.claim: ARY already created a photocopy revenue SKU and never used it once. ProductID 0A32 'Xerox Charges' exists and is active, with zero sale lines in 1,088,607 lifetime bills.
findings.evidence: ary query "SELECT COUNT(*) AS lines, ISNULL(SUM(FinalSaleAmount),0) AS amt FROM SaleDetail WHERE ProductID='0A32'" -> lines 0, amt 0
findings.soWhat: Someone at ARY already decided print/copy belongs in the catalogue. The gap is execution and a machine, not strategy or a new idea to sell internally.

findings.claim: ARY also created a delivery-fee SKU and never used it. ProductID 0BVD 'Delivery Charges' is active with zero sale lines ever.
findings.evidence: Same query, ProductID IN ('0A32','0BVD','0C19','0BO0','07NL') -> 0BVD: 0 lines, ₹0
findings.soWhat: An in-campus delivery service was contemplated and never launched, even though 54.4% of footfall crushes into the 17:00-20:00 window.

findings.claim: Tailoring is a real, running service — 18 named contract tailors on their own ledger group 'Stiching Charges Payable' (group 508), a customer-facing revenue SKU (07NL 'Stiching Charges From Customer'), and a Direct Expenses cost account.
findings.evidence: ary query "SELECT AccountID, AccountName FROM AccountMaster WHERE GroupID=508" -> 18 rows (Anita-Tailor, Kuldeep Kaur - Tailor, Balwinder Singh Tailor, ...); ProductMaster 07NL in ProductGroupID=1
findings.soWhat: The operating model for an outsourced, per-piece service is already built and proven inside ARY. Every other service can be bolted onto this same pattern instead of being designed from scratch.

findings.claim: Tailoring is priced at cost: +₹45,511 gross on ₹15,79,023 of revenue across 3.4 years = 2.9% gross margin, versus the 35-50% a captive alteration desk should earn. FY25-26 was an outright loss of ₹51,324.
findings.evidence: Revenue: SUM(SaleDetail.FinalSaleAmount) WHERE ProductID='07NL' by FY. Cost: SUM(Debit)-SUM(Credit) on AccountMaster.AccountName IN ('Stiching Charges','Stiching Exp.') by FY (both are group 30 Direct Expenses, so tailor cost is expensed, not capitalised into garment stock).
findings.soWhat: The single cheapest margin gain available. No capex, no licence, no new counter — just a price reset in a market with no competing tailor within 30-50 km.

findings.claim: I initially measured the tailoring cost from the tailors' payable ledger (group 508) and got a worse answer (-₹1.24 L cumulative). That was wrong — group 508 mixes in opening balances and receipts. The Direct Expenses accounts are the correct cost measure and give +₹45,511.
findings.evidence: Group 508 voucher-type breakdown: Journal ₹15,25,741 Cr / Opening Balance ₹45,790 / Receipt ₹1,31,398 — i.e. the payable ledger is not a P&L measure. Contra-leg query showed the expense lands on 'Stiching Charges' and 'Stiching Exp.', both group 30 Direct Expenses.
findings.soWhat: Reported because the wrong number would have justified an aggressive price rise on a false premise. Tailoring is break-even, not loss-making.

findings.claim: Stitching attaches to only 13.9% of the fabric ARY sells — the largest single service gap in the business, and it sits inside a category ARY already dominates.
findings.evidence: FY26-27 to 21-Aug: 1,341 distinct bills containing a line from ProductGroupID IN (183 Unstiched Suits, 124 Fabrics, 165 Fabric); 705 bills containing ProductID 07NL; 187 bills containing both.
findings.soWhat: Fabric + unstitched suits ran ₹16.07 L in 4.7 months (~₹41 L/yr). Taking attach from 13.9% to 35% at a normal 35% GM turns ₹22 k/yr of gross profit into roughly ₹6.8 L/yr.

findings.claim: Himachal Pradesh has an officially notified rate card for exactly these services, and it includes printing and scanning. A Lok Mitra Kendra may charge ₹25 per G2C application, ₹5/page B&W print, ₹15/page colour print, ₹5/page scanning, ₹10/page Nakal Jamabandi, ₹25 per G2B application; HPSEB pays ₹5 per domestic bill collected (₹10 commercial).
findings.evidence: https://himseva.hp.gov.in/pages/staticSite/Rate%20List%20of%20LMK%20Charges%20for%20G2C%20Services.pdf — 8-page notified rate list, 74 numbered G2C/EoDB services, '*LMK User Charges' table on the final page. (HP e-District was renamed the HimSeva Portal; edistrict.hp.gov.in now redirects there.)
findings.soWhat: The state has already set the price ARY may charge, which removes the pricing argument entirely and gives the print/copy business a government-sanctioned rate card plus 74 chargeable government services on top.

findings.claim: The AePS / banking-correspondent thesis is dead on arrival: there are TWO full bank branches at Baru Sahib itself, both with NEFT, RTGS, IMPS and UPI live.
findings.evidence: razorpay/ifsc dataset v2.0.61 IFSC.csv (36.3 MB, grep 'BARU'): 'State Bank of India,SBIN0011784,BARU SAHIB,...,VILL AND P O BARU SAHIB,DISTT SIRMAUR,HIMACHAL PRADESH 173101' and 'Punjab National Bank,PUNB0975500,GURUDWARA BARU SAHIB,RAJGARH,...,VPO BARU SAHIB, TEH RAJGARH, DISTT SIRMAUR HP 173101' — both IMPS/RTGS/NEFT/UPI true.
findings.soWhat: The '30-50 km to the nearest market' framing does not extend to banking. Cash-out demand that would justify a micro-ATM largely does not exist; only the after-hours and surrounding-village slice survives.

findings.claim: Baru Sahib's postal infrastructure, by contrast, IS weak — it has only a Branch Post Office, the smallest single-handed unit. Of the 16 post offices sharing PIN 173101, exactly one is a Sub Post Office (Rajgarh) and fifteen are Branch Post Offices.
findings.evidence: https://api.postalpincode.in/pincode/173101 -> 16 PostOffice records; 'Baru Sahib' BranchType 'Branch Post Office', Block Pachhad, Division Solan; only 'Rajgarh (Siramur)' is BranchType 'Sub Post Office'.
findings.number: 1 Sub PO, 15 Branch POs in PIN 173101
findings.soWhat: Courier and parcel is the genuinely underserved logistics gap, not banking — and it is the one every residential-school parent and hostel student feels monthly.

findings.claim: Residents are already digitally native, which guts the mobile-recharge case. Paytm/UPI is 56.3% of all tender lines and 42.9% of value in FY26-27.
findings.evidence: SalePayment joined to ModeOfPayment, VoucherDate>='2026-04-01': Paytm 96,593 lines / ₹1,62,94,274; Cash 69,791 / ₹1,22,78,943; Credit Sale 5,192 / ₹94,32,897. Total ₹3.80 Cr.
findings.soWhat: People who pay by UPI recharge their own phones. Assisted recharge is a near-zero-margin courtesy here, not a revenue line — include it only as a free rider on a CSC licence.

findings.claim: Footfall is large and violently concentrated in the evening: ~36,650 bills/month in FY26-27, with 54.4% of all bills struck between 17:00 and 20:00 and a second spike at 09:00.
findings.evidence: SaleHeader monthly counts Apr-Aug FY26-27: 37,085 / 41,388 / 38,563 / 29,576 / 22,269(to 21 Aug). Hourly DATEPART(hour,DateTimeIn) FY26-27: 17h 22,268; 18h 20,670; 19h 26,269; 20h 22,641 of 168,881 total.
findings.number: ~36,650 bills/month; 91,848 of 168,881 bills in 4 evening hours
findings.soWhat: Any service counter must be staffed 17:00-20:00, and the same window is why an in-campus delivery/order-ahead service would relieve a real queue rather than invent a need.

findings.claim: The print/copy adjacency is already proven by traffic: 7,709 bills touched the Stationary category in 4.7 months (~1,640/month, ₹5.35 L), so the people who need photocopying are already standing at the counter.
findings.evidence: SaleDetail joined ProductGroupMaster, VoucherDate>='2026-04-01', ProductGroupID IN (148,181,124,183,165,161): Stationary 7,709 bills / ₹5,35,316; Academy Dress 1,195 / ₹18,86,923; Unstiched Suits 488 / ₹9,55,391; Fabrics 853 / ₹6,52,307.
findings.soWhat: Zero customer-acquisition cost for a print desk — it converts existing stationery footfall, and stationery buyers are the exact population that photocopies.

findings.claim: A third service SKU was tried and abandoned: 0C19 'Cabin Booking' billed 119 lines / ₹6,070 in FY23-24 and has produced nothing since.
findings.evidence: Service-SKU sales by FY: Cabin Booking fy_start 2023 only, 119 lines, ₹6,070; no rows for later years. 0BO0 'Gift Packing' is the one that stuck: 3,616 lines, ₹52,835 lifetime.
findings.soWhat: ARY has a pattern of launching a service SKU and letting it die. Whatever killed Cabin Booking (staffing? no owner?) will kill the next one unless a named person owns the service line.

findings.claim: Mobile repair is genuinely unserved and adjacent to a category ARY already lists: its entire 'Mobile' product group is 8 SKUs, all of them chargers — no handsets, no accessories of substance, no repair.
findings.evidence: ary query "SELECT ProductID, ProductName, IsActive FROM ProductMaster WHERE ProductGroupID=139" -> 8 rows: Gold Charger 02, Gold Charger 5 In 1, Kish Charger Gold, Atek Charger 5 In 1, Charger 38, Charger 41, Charger 5 In 1, Charger Pin 01
findings.soWhat: 5,000 residents demonstrably carry smartphones (56% UPI tenders) with the nearest repair shop 30-50 km of hill road away. Screen and battery repair is the highest-margin service on this list.

findings.claim: The CSC/Digital Seva route would give ARY a bundle it cannot assemble piecemeal: CSC is itself a BBPOU (so Bharat BillPay for electricity, water, gas, DTH, broadband, landline), is partnered with 42 banks for BC-agent/Customer Service Point work, and carries mobile recharge for 14 telcos, DTH for 6 operators, PAN, Passport, FASTag and e-District.
findings.evidence: csc.gov.in/governmenttocitizen and /financialinclusion (via Wayback, snapshots 2023-05-19 and 2023-12-05 — the live pages currently 500 with 'Unable to load the requested file: gtoc.php'). csc.gov.in/vle (live): '5.4 lakh VLEs, of which 4.35 lakh are in Gram Panchayats'.
findings.number: 42 partner banks; 14 telcos; 6 DTH operators; 5.4 lakh VLEs
findings.soWhat: One licence unlocks a dozen small fee lines at once. Caveat: the service counts and application volumes on those pages date to 2016-17, and Himachal Pradesh was NOT among the 11 states whose e-District was integrated with Digital Seva — in HP the channel is the state's own Lok Mitra Kendra.

findings.claim: Only 296-432 distinct named customers transact per month; 97% of bills go to the single walk-in account 00001. There is no per-resident identity on which to run a subscription or a billed service today.
findings.evidence: SaleHeader FY26-27 GROUP BY month WHERE CustomerID<>'00001': Apr 296 / May 345 / Jun 373 / Jul 432 / Aug 303 distinct customers.
findings.soWhat: Laundry, print accounts, delivery subscriptions and monthly service billing all need a named account. The 3,604 'Akal Academy Cs' ledger accounts are the rail — but they are barely used at the till, so this is a prerequisite, not a detail.

findings.claim: Counter economics point to where a service desk goes: Ary Pos carries 104,491 bills / ₹1.92 Cr in FY26-27, while Ary Clothing does only 4,623 bills but ₹53 L at a ₹1,146 average bill.
findings.evidence: SaleDetail joined WarehouseMaster, VoucherDate>='2026-04-01': Ary Pos 104,491/₹1,91,66,715; Ary Clothing 4,623/₹52,99,903; Basement 9/₹51,38,246; Fruits & Vegetables 24,807/₹26,99,620; Ary G Canteen 20,250/₹23,69,215; Ary Lite 14,701/₹7,36,582.
findings.number: Ary Clothing avg bill ₹1,146 vs Ary Pos ₹183
findings.soWhat: Tailoring and alteration belong at Ary Clothing where the ticket is 6x higher and the customer is already buying fabric; print/copy/courier belong at Ary Pos where the traffic is. Note Basement is wholesale, not retail — 9 bills for ₹51 L.

findings.claim: Tailors are settled up, so the thin tailoring margin is not a timing artefact — net payable to all 18 tailors is -₹3,388 (a slight overpayment).
findings.evidence: SUM(CreditAmount)-SUM(DebitAmount) over TransactionChild for AccountMaster.GroupID=508, IsDeleted=0 -> -3,388
findings.soWhat: Removes the obvious objection that the low margin is just unbilled work in progress. The pricing really is at cost.

findings.claim: India Post Franchise Outlet commission rates could not be verified — indiapost.gov.in's franchise pages 404 on both the legacy .aspx path and the new Next.js route, and no Wayback snapshot exists for them.
findings.evidence: HTTP 404 on https://www.indiapost.gov.in/VAS/Pages/Content/Franchise-Scheme.aspx, /VAS/Pages/Franchise.aspx and /business-services/franchise-scheme; archive.org/wayback/available returns {} (no snapshots) for the franchise page.
findings.soWhat: The courier recommendation is therefore built on a private-carrier aggregation model (Delhivery/DTDC handling fee), not on postal franchise commission. Someone should confirm the postal route with the Solan divisional office before committing.

findings.claim: NPCI's actual AePS interchange is not public. The consolidated interchange circular is restricted, and NPCI blocks automated fetches.
findings.evidence: NPCI AePS circular index (via Wayback 2025-09-19) lists 'NPCI/2017-18/AEPS/01 - Circular 18a Consolidated circular on Switching Fee/ Interchange/ MDR on Aadhaar Based Transaction' with the access note 'Please get in touch with your bank' — no download link. www.npci.org.in returns HTTP 403 to curl even with a browser user-agent; the public AePS Product-Booklet.pdf contains no fee table; Circulars 19(a) and 25(a) download but are scanned images with no text layer.
findings.soWhat: Any AePS commission figure quoted to ARY should be treated as a sponsor bank's offer, not an industry rate. Since the two on-campus branches already sink this idea, it does not need resolving.

findings.claim: AePS mechanics and scope are confirmed even though the pricing is not: it is a bank-led model requiring an authorised Business Correspondent or bank agent, supporting balance enquiry, cash withdrawal, cash deposit, Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar transfer, mini statement and merchant purchase.
findings.evidence: https://www.digitalindia.gov.in/initiative/aeps/ (page last updated 27 Aug 2026)
findings.soWhat: Confirms ARY cannot do this alone — it needs a sponsor bank or a CSC/BC network. Given SBI and PNB are both on campus, the sponsor is more likely to see ARY as a competitor than a partner.

findings.claim: Baru Sahib's institutional scale supports a print/documentation business: Akal Academy has ~1,538 students in an 11-storey building, Eternal University runs 24 programmes with hostels across colleges of Basic Sciences, Agriculture and Nursing, and the Trust network spans 129 CBSE schools with ~60,000 students.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baru_Sahib (Akal Academy 1,538 students; Eternal University 24 programmes; 129 schools; ~60,000 students; 400 acres purchased 1956). eternaluniversity.edu.in confirms residential hostels and names 'Apple a Day' as the campus food outlet — which matches ARY's own 'Ary Apple A Day' counter.
findings.soWhat: A 129-school head office generates continuous forms, circulars, exam papers and admission documentation. The print opportunity is institutional, not just retail — and institutional volume is what pays off a copier.

findings.claim: Total realistic contribution from the recommended service set is roughly ₹2.0-2.2 L/month (~₹25 L/yr), about 2.8% of ARY's ~₹8.96 Cr annualised revenue but at far higher margin than merchandise.
findings.evidence: Sum of the per-service estimates in the sizing table below; derived, not observed. Only the tailoring component rests on verified ARY history.
findings.soWhat: Services will not move ARY's top line much. They defend the captive relationship, lift basket size and fix a margin leak — that is the case for them, and overselling them as a growth engine would be wrong.

recommendations.action: Reprice tailoring and drive fabric→stitching attach from 13.9% to 35%. Nothing needs to be bought: the 18 tailors, the revenue SKU (07NL), the cost account and the Ary Clothing counter all exist. Set a per-garment price card that clears a 35% gross margin, and make the till prompt for stitching on every fabric/unstitched-suit line. Captive market — no competing tailor within 30-50 km — so the price will hold.
recommendations.blocker: Confirm the 18 tailors' commercial terms — are they independent piece-rate contractors whose rates ARY can reset, or Trust-affiliated workers whose rates are fixed by someone else?

recommendations.action: Launch the print/copy/scan desk that ARY already has a SKU for. Activate 0A32 'Xerox Charges', put a multifunction copier at Ary Pos (rent first at ₹4-6k/month + per-copy rather than buying, so the volume assumption gets tested cheaply), and add lamination, spiral binding and passport photos. Price against the HP notified card (₹5/page B&W, ₹15 colour, ₹5 scan) for one-off jobs and ₹1.50-2/page for bulk. Convert the 1,640 stationery bills/month already walking past.
recommendations.blocker: Whether the Akal Academy / Eternal University administration already runs a photocopy facility for students and staff. If it does, this number roughly halves and the play becomes an institutional print contract instead of a retail counter.

recommendations.action: Add mobile repair — screen and battery replacement plus a real accessories range. ARY's entire mobile category is 8 charger SKUs, while 56% of its tender lines are UPI, so every resident carries a smartphone and the nearest repair is 30-50 km of hill road away. Start with a technician visiting two days a week on revenue share before hiring.
recommendations.blocker: Sourcing a competent technician willing to work at Baru Sahib; spares supply chain from Solan/Chandigarh.

recommendations.action: Open a courier and parcel desk. This is the one genuine logistics gap: Baru Sahib has only a Branch Post Office and the nearest Sub Post Office is Rajgarh. Sign a Delhivery or DTDC pickup/drop arrangement and run an inbound parcel hold-and-notify service for hostel students, charging ₹20-30 handling. Start with inbound holding, which needs no carrier agreement at all — just shelving, a scanner and a register.
recommendations.blocker: Carrier willingness to serve PIN 173101 daily; hill-road pickup frequency is the real constraint, not the agreement.

recommendations.action: Apply for a Lok Mitra Kendra licence via the HimSeva portal. It pays ₹25 per G2C application across 74 notified services, ₹5 per HPSEB domestic bill collected, and — importantly — it puts ARY's print and scan charges on an officially notified rate card. The catchment is not just the 5,000 campus residents but the 15 surrounding Branch-Post-Office villages.
recommendations.blocker: Whether an LMK is already allotted for Baru Sahib or the Rajgarh block — allotments are typically exclusive by area. Check before investing effort.

recommendations.action: Activate SKU 0BVD 'Delivery Charges' and run in-campus delivery in the 17:00-20:00 window, where 54.4% of all bills already land. Charge ₹20 a drop. Judge it on basket size and queue relief for staff families with small children, not on the fee — the fee will never pay for itself alone.
recommendations.blocker: No per-resident identity at the till: 97% of bills go to the single walk-in account 00001 and only ~350 named customers transact monthly. Delivery needs an address and a name.

recommendations.action: Build the named-customer rail before any subscription or billed service. The 3,604 'Akal Academy Cs' ledger accounts exist but are barely used at the counter. Without a resident identity on the bill, laundry accounts, print accounts, delivery and monthly service billing are all impossible to operate or measure.
recommendations.blocker: Till workflow and staff habit — cashiers default to the cash account because it is faster at a 1,200-bill day.

recommendations.action: Scope laundry and dry cleaning as an agency, not a plant — collection point at ARY, processing at a Solan or Nahan facility. Aim at winter wear and staff-family laundry rather than student uniforms, which the Trust probably already handles.
recommendations.blocker: Find out whether the Trust already runs institutional laundry for its ~1,538 boarders. If it does, the addressable market is only staff families and dry cleaning.

recommendations.action: Do NOT invest in AePS or a banking-correspondent setup as a standalone play. Baru Sahib already has two full bank branches on campus (SBI SBIN0011784 and PNB PUNB0975500), both with UPI, NEFT, RTGS and IMPS. If a micro-ATM ever goes in, justify it only on after-hours access — banks shut at 16:00 while 54% of ARY's footfall is 17:00-20:00 — and on the surrounding villages, not on campus demand.
recommendations.blocker: none — the recommendation is to not spend

recommendations.action: Treat mobile/DTH recharge and BBPS as free riders on the CSC licence, never as a reason to buy anything. Residents already self-serve: Paytm is 56.3% of tender lines. Same for LPG booking, which now carries no fee at all — offer it as goodwill.

Ask why 'Cabin Booking' (SKU 0C19) died after ₹6,070 in FY23-24, and assign a single named owner to each new service line before launch. ARY's own history shows the failure mode is not bad ideas — it is unowned SKUs: two service SKUs have zero lifetime sales and a third was abandoned.

openQuestions: Does the Akal Academy / Eternal University administration already run a photocopy and printing facility for its students and staff? This is the single biggest swing factor — it would halve the print estimate and turn a retail counter into an institutional print contract. Ask the ARY manager or the Trust's campus administration.
Does the Trust already run institutional laundry for the ~1,538 residential-school boarders? Determines whether laundry is a real opportunity or only a staff-family/dry-cleaning niche.

Are the 18 tailors on ledger group 508 independent piece-rate contractors whose rates ARY can reset, or Trust-affiliated workers on fixed rates? The whole tailoring repricing recommendation depends on this. Ask the Ary Clothing counter in-charge.

Why was 'Cabin Booking' (0C19) abandoned after FY23-24, and what was it actually booking — guest rooms, a hall, transport? Someone at ARY knows, and the answer probably predicts what will kill the next service SKU.

Is a Lok Mitra Kendra already allotted for Baru Sahib or the Rajgarh block, and what is the current LMK application procedure? The 'How to apply for LMK' link on himseva.hp.gov.in is JavaScript-driven and did not resolve to a document. The HP District e-Governance Society, Sirmaur (Nahan) would know.

Can an India Post Franchise Outlet be opened at Baru Sahib given a departmental Branch Post Office already exists there? The franchise scheme's eligibility rules could not be retrieved — indiapost.gov.in 404s on every franchise path and has no Wayback snapshot. Confirm with the Solan postal division.
Is there an ATM at Baru Sahib (either bank's), and what are the SBI and PNB branch working hours? This decides whether the after-hours cash argument for a micro-ATM has anything left in it.

What is Eternal University's current student headcount and how many live in hostels? Their website carries testimonials but no enrolment figure, and this is a direct multiplier on the print, courier and laundry estimates.

Do staff families in campus quarters hold individual HPSEB domestic connections, or does the Trust hold bulk connections? The ₹5-per-bill HPSEB collection commission is worth nothing if there are no individual bills.

What did the surrounding-village catchment look like historically — do residents of the 15 nearby Branch-Post-Office villages already shop at ARY? Sales are booked 97% to one anonymous walk-in account, so the data cannot answer this; the counter staff can.
confidenceGap: Every internal figure here was pulled live from FR8HODBNEW and is solid, and the Himachal LMK rate card is an official government notification — but every revenue number for a service ARY has never run is a model, not an observation. ARY has operated exactly one service at scale (tailoring), so there is no internal precedent to calibrate attach rates or per-resident consumption against. Two specific unknowns could each move the total by 25% or more: whether the Academy/University already provides photocopying on campus (halves the largest new line) and whether the Trust already runs laundry. A process caveat worth stating plainly: this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before my first call, so the external research was done by scraping Bing, the Wayback Machine, a text proxy and official sites directly with curl. That worked well for government sources — it is how the HP LMK rate card, the postal hierarchy and the two bank branches got verified — but it failed on commercial commission rates, which is why India Post franchise terms and NPCI's AePS interchange are reported as NOT-CHECKED rather than guessed at.
